after.name: Question 1
after.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x={t}^{2}-2,\,y=2{t}^{4}+5$ where $t$ is a real number. Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
after.worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=2t,\,{y}^{′}(t)=8{t}^{3}.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{8{t}^{3}}{2t}=4{t}^{2}.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(4{t}^{2})}{2t} \\  & =\frac{8t}{2t} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1.$ Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
after.worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{y}^{′}(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}=2\operatorname{cot}⁡t.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(2\operatorname{cot}⁡t)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\  & =-\frac{2{csc}^{2}⁡t}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\  & =-2{csc}^{3}⁡t.\end{aligned}

content.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1.$ Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
content.worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{y}^{′}(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}=2\operatorname{cot}⁡t.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(2\operatorname{cot}⁡t)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\  & =-\frac{2{csc}^{2}⁡t}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\  & =-2{csc}^{3}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$
